newsitem.title: USA: Morgan Stanley net rises on strong investment banking fees.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley net rises on strong investment banking fees.

text.p: Morgan Stanley Group Inc. Wednesday said its earnings rose 5 percent in the latest quarter despite sluggishness in the stock market over much of the summer.
The nation's biggest brokerage in the mergers and acquisitions field cited strong investment banking revenues and higher fees from trading for its own account.
It also said president John Mack was named to the additional post of chief executive officer.

Morgan Stanley said net income rose to $219 million, or $1.32 a share, in the quarter ended Aug. 31, from $209 million, or $1.23 a share, in the comparable 1995 quarter. Net revenues grew 12 percent to $1.29 billion from $1.15 billion.
The results were a penny above expectations, according to First Call, and Morgan Stanley stock added 62.5 cents to $51.875 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
"We are pleased by the firm's strong performance during the quarter despite lower levels of client activity in many of our key businesses," Chairman Richard Fisher and Mack said in a joint statement.

The company also said that Mack will assume the additional post of chief executive officer effective June 1, 1997. Fisher will continue as chairman. "This is the expected next step in our succession plan," Fisher said.

After record levels of activity in the first half of its fiscal year, less-favourable market conditions prevailed in the third quarter, the company said. But its mix of businesses helped boost sales and earnings from the year-ago period.
Investment banking revenues of $431 million in the quarter, up from $355 million in the 1995 quarter, were the third-best in the firm's history, it said.
Trading revenues grew 21 percent to $427 million from $352 million.
Asset management fees of $137 million were up substantially, reflecting revenues from Miller Anderson & Sherrerd LLP, which Morgan Stanley acquired in January.
Morgan Stanley is also acquiring Van Kampen American Capital, another asset management firm, and expects to complete the deal in its fourth quarter.

For the nine months, earnings jumped 88 percent, largely on a big increase in investment banking fees, to $793 million, or $4.79 a share, from $422 million, or $2.41 a share, in the prior period. Revenues net of interest expense rose 44 percent to $4.26 billion from $2.96 billion.
